newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU approves more oilseed varieties for area aid.
newsitem.headline: EU approves more oilseed varieties for area aid.

text.p: About 80 oilseed varieties will be added to an approved list eligible for European Union subsidies under area aid schemes, an EU member state official said on Monday.
The oilseed varieties have already been approved at national level.
The official added that the European Commission is likely to propose an extension of the area aid planting deadline for French buckwheat by two weeks until the end of May.

The official, speaking after a meeting of EU grain experts last week, said that France requested the extension, which would apply to less than 1,000 hectares in Brittany, because wet conditions delay planting.
Sweden also wants to extend the planting deadline for three Swedish counties by two weeks until mid-June due to long winters.

Separately, Greece requested an increase of 19,764 hectares in its irrigated cereals and oilseed area eligible to EU aid. The increase would cover irrigation projects started, but not completed, before August 1992.

In response, the European Commission requested Greece to propose changes to its regional cereals and oilseed area aid programmes to ensure that the overall historic yield upon which EU subsidy payments are based, remains unchanged.
